citeAs: Antol, S., Agrawal, A., Lu, J., Mitchell, M., Batra, D., Zitnick, C. L., and Parikh, D. (2015). VQA: Visual Question Answering. The IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV).
creator: Stanislaw Antol, Aishwarya Agrawal, Jiasen Lu, Margaret Mitchell, Dhruv Batra, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Devi Parikh
description: The VQA Dataset consists of real images from the COCO dataset (COCO-VQA) and abstract synthetic cartoon images (SYNTH-VQA). COCO-VQA contains 614,163 question-answer pairs across 204,721 images, with three questions per image and ten answers per question, collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk. It supports both open-ended and multiple-choice evaluation formats.
name: VQA (The VQA Dataset / COCO-VQA)
rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 answers per question (10 independent annotators per question); 3 questions per image
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is approximately 83.3% using the AccuracyVQA metric. Inter-human agreement is especially poor for 'Why' questions, with over 59% of these questions having fewer than three annotators giving exactly the same answer. More than 13% of 'yes/no' answers have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AMT workers were asked to generate questions designed to 'Stump a smart robot' for each image. A separate pool of workers provided answers to those questions. For multiple-choice format, 18 choices were provided: the correct answer (most frequent answer from 10 annotators), 3 plausible answers (collected without seeing the image), 10 popular answers (top answers in the dataset), and random correct answers for other questions.
rai:dataBiases: COCO-VQA has strong language biases: image-blind algorithms achieve 49.6% accuracy using only the question. 'Yes/no' answers span about 38% of all questions, and almost 59% of them are answered with 'yes.' The dataset contains many subjective, opinion-seeking questions without a single objective answer. Questions beginning with 'Is there' can be answered 'yes' with 85.2% accuracy. The dataset also contains many questions that can be answered without examining the image due to language priors.
rai:dataCollection: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each COCO image by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot.' A separate pool of workers were hired to generate answers to the questions. Each question was answered by 10 independent annotators. For SYNTH-VQA, questions and answers were collected for 50,000 synthetic cartoon scenes.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real images from the Microsoft COCO dataset (204,721 images) and 50,000 synthetic cartoon scenes depicting different simulated scenarios made from over 100 different objects, 30 different animal models, and 20 human cartoon models.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataLimitations: COCO-VQA has strong language biases that allow algorithms to perform well without truly understanding images. The dataset contains subjective and opinion-seeking questions that lack definitive answers. Inter-human agreement is only 83.3%, making 100% accuracy impossible. The evaluation metric (AccuracyVQA) can inflate scores; answering 'yes' to all yes/no questions yields 71% accuracy. The dataset does not provide a detailed breakdown of question types, making it difficult to evaluate performance on specific question categories.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA systems enabled by this dataset can serve as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals, enabling them to get information about images on the web and in the real world. More generally, VQA could improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating VQA algorithms; benchmarking image understanding systems; aiding blind and visually impaired individuals; improving human-computer interaction; image retrieval; serving as a component of a Visual Turing Test for image understanding.
